To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

teachers' mathematical knowledge and understanding are related to their teaching practices and to their students' mathematical performance, and that these relationships are positive, that is, the more mathematics teachers know, the better they teach, and the better they teach the better their students learn.

(a) teachers' knowledge of mathematics is related to their students' achievement in mathematics; (b) teachers' knowledge is not strongly related to their students'' achievement in reading or writing, nor does it seem likely to be; (c) teachers' knowledge can and does improve with in service professional development;

(1) the mathematics teachers know is not what they need to know to teach mathematics effectively; (2) what mathematics teachers need to know to be effective is different from what they know; and (3) what they need to learn is more difficult to learn than they think.
